title: Nuclear fuel chain
eyebrow: Product-chain pilot · the fuel behind the reactor
h1: The uranium mine is the easy part — the chokepoint is a service, not a rock
deck: Nuclear fuel is not just uranium ore. Between the mine and the reactor sit conversion, enrichment and fabrication — industrial services, not commodities. The mine is diversified and buffered by stockpiles; the concentration is downstream, and at enrichment Russia is the single largest supplier.
correction: Worrying about 'who has the uranium' misreads the chain. Uranium is mined across Kazakhstan, Canada, Namibia, Australia and Niger, and utilities hold years of stock. The binding steps are the services: conversion sits with four suppliers, enrichment is led by Russia's Rosatom, and fuel fabrication must be licensed to a specific reactor. The rock is fungible; the service is not.

sections.h2: 1 · The mine is diversified — and cushioned

panels.h3: Many producers, plus a stockpile buffer
panels.text: Kazakhstan leads at ~43% of mine output, but Canada, Namibia, Australia and Niger supply the rest, and known resources are widely spread. Crucially, uranium is cheap to store and utilities and governments hold multi-year inventories, so a mine disruption does not stop a reactor the way a cut-off in an industrial service would. The mine is the least fragile link.

panels.h3: The reactor locks in the fuel
panels.text: A fuel assembly is engineered and licensed to a particular reactor design, so a utility cannot freely switch fabricators or, historically, enrichers. That is why Russian-designed VVER reactors across Europe were hard to de-Russify quickly — the dependence is embedded in the machine, not just the fuel market.

sections.h2: 2 · Conversion and enrichment are the chokepoints

panels.note: OECD NEA. Turning yellowcake into UF6 gas for enrichment is done at a handful of plants: Rosatom, Cameco, CNNC and Orano together hold nearly all of it. This is a services oligopoly, not a commodity market — and it is a deliberately narrow neck between a diversified mine and a Russia-led enrichment stage.

panels.text: Enrichment, a service measured in separative-work units, is even more concentrated, with Russia the single largest supplier. The next-generation twist is HALEU (high-assay low-enriched uranium) that many advanced and small modular reactors need — and today Russia is essentially the only commercial source, so a new reactor class is being designed around a supply that barely exists outside one country.
panels.flag: the new reactors need a fuel almost only Russia makes

panels.text: Most chains in this atlas concentrate at a mine or a refinery. Nuclear concentrates at engineered services — conversion plants, enrichment centrifuges, licensed fabrication — that take a decade and heavy capital to build. The West is now rebuilding exactly this capacity (new enrichment in the US, UK, France) precisely because the rock was never the problem.
panels.flag: rebuilding a service, not opening a mine

trade_intro: BACI carries uranium ore and compounds, but enrichment and conversion are traded as services and under long confidential contracts that customs data does not capture. Read any uranium trade below as ore movement only — the real chokepoints (enrichment SWU, licensed fabrication) are invisible in trade statistics.
